text: The project was delayed due to a shortage of engineers.
The tariff was frozen. As a result, investors lost confidence.
Despite the crisis, the port doubled its exports.
The root cause was an incomplete design.

I know everybody wants to know why the airport opened two years late. The weather was not the reason. The root cause was the design of the terminal, which was not complete when we signed the contract. Because the design changed three times, the environmental license had to be reviewed. That review triggered an eight-month delay. As a result, we lost the window for the main construction work, and costs went up. Although the delay was long, the final terminal is bigger and safer than the original. Despite everything, passenger numbers in the first year were higher than expected.

Freezing tariffs is always popular. Users pay less, and politicians win votes. But there is a side effect. Because the concessionaire receives less money, it cuts investment in maintenance. As a result, the quality of the service falls after two or three years. There is also a knock-on effect on new projects: investors see the freeze and ask for higher returns everywhere in the country. So although the decision helps users today, it often costs them more tomorrow. In my view, the long-term costs usually outweigh the short-term benefits.
The project was delayed due to a shortage of engineers.
The tariff was frozen. As a result, investors lost confidence.
Despite the crisis, the port doubled its exports.
The license was late because the agency had no staff.
Most delays stem from decisions made at the beginning.
The root cause was an incomplete design.
